# Jev decision bench — 2026-09-30 10:50

Three backends compared on the same harness (tests/bench/jev-bench.py — 10
confirm-gate noul cases + 8 tool-routing choice cases).

## Results

| backend | where | model | confirm-gate | tool-route | accuracy | latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| jev-student | idc01:8778 | distilbert-multilingual FT (v1, 1.3k turns) | **8/10** | n/a (binary-only) | 8/10 confirm | **~0.1s** |
| open-jev (1b) | idc01:8777 | gemma-3-1b-it torch | 5/10 | 5/8 | 10/18 (56%) | ~4.8s |
| open-jev (4b) | tony-omen:8777 | gemma-3-4b-it torch (down — RAM) | ~9/10 | ~7/8 | ~89% (est) | 25-40s |

## Student model

- **Arch**: `distilbert-base-multilingual-cased` sequence-classification head,
  fine-tuned 4 epochs on 1,293 deduped labeled turns (live corpus +
  transcript-mined corpus; 219 True / 1074 False, class-weighted CE).
- **Val**: n=194 acc=0.985 prec=0.92 rec=1.00 @ noul threshold 0.70.
- **Deploy**: `jev-student.service` on idc01:8778, ~520MB ckpt, CPU-only.
- **Misses** (fail-safe direction — real affirmation scored low):
  "yes, publish it" p=0.030, "go ahead" p=0.030. Bare "Yes" p=0.955.
  English imperative-shaped affirmations are under-trained.
- **Junk correctly rejected**: 연연/준연/中文 p≈0.02 — the new regex
  foreign-script gate and the student agree.

## Notes

- Student does binary noul only; the 8 tool-routing cases score 0 by
  design (returns a fixed 'answer' stub).
- 4b on tony-omen is down (18GB RSS on a 30G box — wedged); its numbers
  are the last healthy baseline, not a re-run.
- Production gate remains the regex — both Jevs are advisory only.

# Benchmark `speaker-enrollment` — 2026-09-28 15:05

Follow-up to the morning's memory-recall benchmark. Motivated by
transcript 2026-09-28-689daaa11c where Tony's enrollment failed twice:
'insufficient audio' on a digit recitation, then 'no buffered audio' —
a dead-ish capture path with no diagnostics.

## What was wrong

- enroll_from_buffer drew only the last ~5s of a 6s ring — an 'ok, enroll
  me' reply left ~1-2s of usable voice; failures looked like user error.
- Unrecognized-speaker audio was consumed by identify() then dropped —
  nothing accrued for a later enrollment.
- Thin profiles (Tony 2 prints, KK 1) made marginal voices miss —
  session fd3d4bdfcb had to re-enroll Tony on the spot.
- 'No buffered audio' conflated 'bridge dead' vs 'user didn't speak'.

## Fixes (commit 242b387 + merge 272e253, backend/speaker_id.py)

- A: _recent ring 6s -> 30s (ADA_SPEAKER_RECENT_S).
- B: auto_learn() — confident hits (>=0.60, ADA_SPEAKER_AUTO_LEARN_MIN)
  append a print; own-voice guard + outlier pruning still apply.
  Profiles now improve with use. Verified live: Tony went 2 -> 3 prints
  during the benchmark run itself.
- C: _pending_voice accrues voiced chunks while the speaker is
  unrecognized; enroll prefers it over the reply tail; cleared on
  attribution so one speaker's accrued voice can't be claimed under
  another name.
- D: enroll_from_buffer reports fed-vs-voiced seconds — 'no audio
  arrived (capture bridge dead; restart)' vs '0.8s voiced — ask for a
  longer natural sentence'.

## Results (live ada-ha-tony :8002, speechbrain ECAPA-TDNN)

- speaker_enrollment (audio tier): PASS — synthetic voice fixture
  unrecognized -> enrolled as 'Guest Tester' -> reconnect -> replayed
  voice correctly identified as Guest Tester. Enrollment source was the
  accrued pending voice, not just the reply.
- speaker_enrollment_sim (text tier): not re-run — text sessions still
  have no audio by design; D now makes the failure diagnostic explicit.
- Unit tests: 23/23 speaker_id, 60/60 memory_banks pass.

## Remaining

- KK still has 1 print — auto_learn will build it as she talks; no
  action needed.
- speaker_remove cleanup 404s on name variants — cosmetic, profile was
  removed.

- mddb vector index: rebuilt 09:47→12:38 (2h45m cold load, 503s

## 4. Speaker-ID structure assessment

Pros: identity enforced below the model; person-scoped banks; draft
quarantine; contamination guard; switch hysteresis; per-sample prints.
Cons: single-channel winner-take-all (no diarization for two-talkers);
no drift detection; retained .pcm clips are a privacy liability vs
vouch's vectors-only stance; profiles file is unversioned single JSON.

GitHub candidates ranked: WeSpeaker AS-Norm/PLDA scoring (biggest
accuracy gain in the borderline band) > drop/encrypt .pcm retention >
drift detection (per-speaker score trend) > streaming diarization
(Sortformer/Diart — big lift, only if multi-speaker is real).


## 5. Notification interruption fix (15:40, commit dc2632a)

Follow-up to the 'Ada stops responding when a data package arrives'
report. /api/notify now splits on an `urgent` body flag:

- non-urgent (default): the client gets a `notify_voice` ws event and
  announces it via speechSynthesis — a flat machine voice, not Ada's.
  Ada receives only a silent context note (turn_complete=False): 'a
  notification arrived, the user was told, don't speak of it now; bring
  it up when the work is done or asked.' She never pauses.
- urgent=true: injected as a user turn immediately — she interrupts and
  announces (urgent + important).
- mid-response notes queue and drain silently at the next turn boundary.

The earlier silent-absorption bug (notify during an in-flight generation
was swallowed) is fixed by the same queue — the note can't be lost
inside a running turn.


## 6. 2026-09-29 follow-up — probe, test isolation, notify scenario

- **mddb-embed-probe.timer** (idc01, every 15min): POSTs /v1/vector-search,
  writes ops-event on up/down transitions. Covers the silent-quota class —
  09-28's OpenRouter-403 + Gemini-429 ran unannounced for ~2h.
- **conftest.py**: pins ADA_INSTANCE_ID=test suite-wide; test_ops_events
  patch.dicts 'tony' at provider construction. Collection-order flakes
  gone — 400/400 pass with and without ambient env.
- **notify_mid_response scenario PASS**: (1) non-urgent arrive mid-turn
  delivers the 'notify_voice' client event and Ada finishes her answer
  untouched; (2) the silent context note is recalled on demand; (3) an
  urgent=true notify interrupts and is verbalized. Session targeting
  added — /api/notify accepts `session`, ready event carries session_id.
  Found en route: turn_complete=False context sends during a turn are
  dropped by the API — notes now always queue and flush on idle or at
  the next boundary.


## 8. 2026-09-30 — retention + drift

- **.pcm TTL** (76455c6): speaker_samples clips expire after
  ADA_SPEAKER_AUDIO_TTL_DAYS=14 — bounded voice-audio retention while
  keeping recent clips for the LOO bench. Vectors-only posture remains
  available via ADA_SPEAKER_KEEP_AUDIO=0.
- **voiceprint drift tracker** (de33415): rolling per-speaker score
  window (12 chunks); mean <0.58 over >=6 samples emits one
  voiceprint_drift ops event per speaker per day — catches stale prints
  / mic changes before misses start. Tied to _emit_ops_event -> chaba

# mddb ops/split structure — 2026-10-02

**Decision: split mddb into leader + ops instances — Ada memory on
idc01, high-volume operational streams on idc02.**

## Why
The leader vector index rebuilds in ~2h on restart (21k docs). Half the
db is `host-logs` (11k) + event streams that are written constantly and
never vector-searched. Splitting them off makes the leader's index
rebuild in minutes and keeps the follower/DR copy lean.

## Structure
- **idc01 `mddb` :11023 (wr)** — banks, cms-pages, ssot, kb. The memory
  brain. ~5k docs, embedded.
- **idc02 `mddb-ops` :11025 (wr)** — host-logs, ada-ha-events-*,
  snapshots, recall-summary, actions, yomi-digest. `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=
  none`; timestamped append-logs, keyword/meta search only.
- **idc02 `mddb-lab` :11024 (wr)** — nightly snapshot replica (existing).
- **tony-dell `mddb` (ro follower)** — replicates the LEADER only; ops
  noise never leaves idc02.

## Ada-side mechanism
One new env `MDDB_OPS_URL` (defaults to `MDDB_BASE_URL` — zero-change
deploy). A second `MddbClient` for ops collections; three call-sites
swap: `event_recorder` (ada-ha-events-*), `tool_runner` snapshots,
`conversation_memory`/`summary_rollups` recall-summary.

## Rules
1. Reads always hit the leader — ops collections are write-only.
2. Ops stream has no embedding — it's telemetry, not memory.
3. Follower tracks leader only — DR copy stays ~2.7G and shrinking.

## Follow-ups
- mddb-ops unit spec on idc02
- repoint writers (log-shipper `LOG_COLLECTION`, digest-to-mddb, probes)
- rebuild leader db via the 2026-09-30 runbook to physically shrink the
  file (bbolt doesn't release pages on delete)

# Jev advisory divergence report (corpus: 2026-09-28 → 2026-10-04)

Source: `~/.local/share/ada/jev-corpus.jsonl` on idc01 (every probed turn = transcript + regex label + Jev noul score).

## Totals

- Probes: **2,928** corpus rows (3,128 log lines incl. pre-corpus)
- Diverged: **71 (2.4%)**
- regex=yes / jev=no: **50** — regex over-fire pattern
- regex=no / jev=yes: **21** — mostly Jev false-positives, a few real regex misses

## regex=yes, jev=no (50) — the actionable half

Regex fires on an affirm *word anywhere* in the turn; Jev requires a standalone or leading affirmation. Real cases:

| text | jev | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `เอ๊ะ! No. อือ อือ ...` (tv_action) | 0.00 | **regex wrong** — explicit No scored as confirm |
| `อย่างงั้น ผม อนุมัติ ได้ เลย ไหม` | 0.01 | regex wrong — *question* about approval |
| `Confirm the camera actually moved — ask it...` | 0.05 | regex wrong — "confirm" used as verb |
| `ต่อได้เลยไม่ต้องรอผมยืนยันแล้ว...` | 0.02 | **regex arguably right** — user grants blanket proceed; Jev rejects embedded affirm |
| `กดสร้างไปเลยแล้วหาข้อมูล...` | 0.04 | embedded affirm in long request — ambiguous |
| `ตกลง` x2 | 0.02 | **jev wrong** — standalone Thai affirmation missed |

Fixable deterministic regex gaps: negation veto (`no`, `ไม่`, `อย่า`), question veto (`?`, `ไหม` ending), `confirm <object>` verb usage.

## regex=no, jev=yes (21) — mostly Jev bias

Jev over-scores Thai imperative+เลย commands ("just do it" ≈ affirmation):

- `สลับเลย` 0.90, `โชว์วิดีโอวอลล์เลย` 0.98, `ออกทริปเลย` 0.97, `ส่งมาเลย` 0.94, `ออกไป` 0.99 (x2)
- `ไม่ใช้ในการบ้านอ่ะ` 0.99 — clear miss
- `Keep the camera running.` 0.98 — command, not confirm

Real regex misses worth noting: `ได้ ส่ง มา เลย` 0.79 (ได้ = okay), `ต้องมาเลย` 0.88.

## Decision input

- Keep regex as enforcer. Jev-as-gate would **fail worse**: it treats plain commands as confirmations (เลย-imperatives at 0.9–0.99) and misses `ตกลง`.
- Jev's value is exactly what we built it for: the 71 divergent rows are a hand-labeled hard-case corpus for the gemma-3-4b fine-tune (notebook already committed).
- Recommended next regex patches (deterministic): negation veto, question-mark/ไหม veto, `confirm <obj>` verb exclusion. Est. kills ~40% of observed over-fires with zero new dependencies.
- Promoting Jev to *second-opinion veto only on regex=yes* is a possible middle path — would have blocked the `No.` misfire, but also blocks legitimate embedded grants like `ต่อได้เลยไม่ต้องรอผมยืนยัน`. Needs the fine-tune first.
